correctness.rationale: The n+1 normalized independent exponentials give the complete endpoint-inclusive spacing vector. For fixed K the perturbation of all heights is bounded by K max(E_j)|n/T−1|=O_P(log(n)/sqrt(n)), and the Erlang survival polynomial gives n times each single-window tail converging to exp(−x) with the specified centering. I checked the critical overlap estimate also for a nested pair: split off h common exponentials, average the two exceedance inequalities and let R be half the sum of the exclusive exponentials, with shape zero meaning no term. Conditioning on R≤z, the Erlang tail is at most C exp(−z)exp(R)(1+z)^(h−1); R>z is bounded by exp(−z)E exp(R). Thus averaging the centered thresholds produces n^−1(log n)^[h−(k+l)/2], with exponent at most −1/2 for distinct windows. In a fixed factorial-moment tuple each support-connected component has only O(n) starts and bounded relative offsets; disjoint components are independent, and any nontrivial component gains the logarithmic loss. Repeated labeled windows cannot arise from factorial moments within one cell or across disjoint cells of that label. For independent placements the first-order probabilities and spatial Riemann sums factor; deleting the O(n^(r−1)) overlapping placements from the order-r independent sum has no effect. Moment determinacy of the limiting Poisson counts, bounded expected masses of compact strips and rectangle approximation give joint vague convergence. The uniform perturbation then transfers convergence using continuous test functions and tight counts on enlarged strips. For top marks, union-bound the unnormalized tails above R and use the uniform perturbation; a count void on [−R,R] vanishes in the iterated limit. Diffuse Poisson heights give unique top points, and the product intensity yields uniform locations independent of heights. The maximal spacing tends to zero and uniform order-statistic deviations give the same spatial limit in physical coordinates. The finite checker provides ingredient diagnostics only and was not executed.
residual_risks: Fixed finite family and uniform sampling only. Arbitrary finite sets of distinct lengths follow by projecting a sufficiently large fixed prefix, not by letting K grow.
No finite-sample independence or quantitative approximation asserted.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The circle theorem materially overlaps the spatial k=2 field after forgetting its extra mark. Cutting at the endpoints changes only a bounded number of gap sums involving the ends; these are bounded sums of at most three normalized exponentials and are individually nonextreme with probability tending to one. The center and left-endpoint positions differ by at most the maximal gap, and rank/n approaches the physical coordinate. Credit the k=2 spatial specialization notwithstanding the circular presentation. Neither comparator is an equivalent joint theorem for several lengths.

value.rationale: The statistics share almost all the same underlying sample and often overlapping windows. The theorem identifies when their extremal dependence disappears even for spatial fields and maximizing locations, not just one set of Gumbel marginals. This supplies joint calibration for arbitrary fixed groups of spacing lengths and an explanation in terms of overlap decay. No claim of added value is made for isolated k=1 or k=2 marginals.
residual_risks: Asymptotic description only; not a guarantee for growing lengths, nonuniform samples or finite-n multiple testing.
